newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM NEAR DEAL WITH SUEZ ON TRACTEBEL STATUS.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM NEAR DEAL WITH SUEZ ON TRACTEBEL STATUS.

text.p: The Belgian government is close to a deal with French Compagnie de Suez about the autonomy of Suez-controlled Belgian utility group Tractebel, Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Tuesday.

"For a number of strategic companies it is important to set up structures for corporate governance. We are in talks with Suez with the aim of a volontary reduction of its influence (in Tractebel). We are close to an agreeement," Dehaene told a Belgian parliamentary committee.
Last month leading Tractebel shareholder Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) , itself majority-owned by Suez, released details about planned statute changes at Tractebel.
They are aimed at boosting Tractebel's independence, partly through the nomination of independent board members.
"The final stage of the talks is now focusing on how one determines whether a board member is independent," Dehaene told Reuters after the committee meeting.

Suez's planned merger with French utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux has led to fears in Belgium that Tractebel's expansion of its international energy and waste management businesses would be thwarted.
"The Suez-Lyonnaise merger does not lead to a change in French influence, although it is true that Suez is changing from a financial holding company into an industrial company," Dehaene said.
He told the committee the government was working on a draft law on so-called autonomous limited companies aimed at strengthening corporate independence.
He gave few details, but referred to the proposed changes in Tractebel's statutes.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
